title: Measures to Minimise Radicalisation in Our Community
what_it_is: Measures to Minimise Radicalisation in Our Community

sections.label: Parliament questions on terrorism threat
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Home Affairs on security of public buildings, self-radicalisation, racial harmony, community partnerships and SGSecure initiatives.

sentences.text: The following question stood in the name of  Miss Cheng Li Hui –   3  To ask	the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what further measures does the Ministry have in place to boost the security of our public buildings, particularly the schools, against the growing threat of terrorist attacks; (b) how can the risk of self-radicalisation be minimised among our students and school staff; and (c) whether there will be more resources committed to raise racial harmony in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the detention of the first female Singaporean for radicalism (a) how can the Home Team enhance its efforts to work with communities in Singapore to reduce the likelihood of Singaporeans becoming radicalised; and (b) whether the Government-community partnership can be further strengthened to increase our readiness to stay united should an attack happen on our shores.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs whether he can give an assessment of the terrorism threat posed by radicalised foreigners in Singapore and what measures are being taken to counter the threat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the recent terrorist attacks in Europe and Asia over the last few months, (a) whether the current SGSecure initiatives are sufficient; and (b) whether there are new initiatives to counter copycats of lone-wolf attacks.

sections.label: Review of public space security
sections.summary: MHA and other agencies are reviewing security measures in public spaces against hostile vehicle attacks, possibly using bollards or barriers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MHA, together with several other agencies, is reviewing existing security measures in public spaces, in particular, against hostile vehicle attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Possible new measures include putting up bollards or security barriers.

sections.label: Event security and infrastructure protection
sections.summary: Organisers of large or higher-risk events must put security measures in place, and a new Infrastructure Protection Act will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Organisers of events that attract large crowds, or are of higher risk, are required to put necessary security measures in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will introduce a new Infrastructure Protection Act later this year − to better protect critical infrastructure and large-scale developments.

sections.label: Radicalised Bangladeshis and foreign domestic workers
sections.summary: About 40 radicalised Bangladeshi nationals were repatriated except six imprisoned, and nine radicalised foreign domestic workers were uncovered since 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2015 and 2016, some 40 Bangladeshi nationals in Singapore were found to have been radicalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They supported the use of violence to pursue their extremist ideology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We repatriated all of them to Bangladesh, except for six who are currently serving prison sentences in Singapore for terrorism financing offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since 2015, we have also uncovered nine cases of radicalised foreign domestic workers (FDWs).

sections.label: Repatriation of radicalised workers
sections.summary: All nine radicalised foreign domestic workers were repatriated to their home countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: All nine of them have been repatriated to their home countries.

sections.label: Religious leaders and NCCS letter
sections.summary: Religious and community leaders must play an active role, and NCCS wrote to MUIS supporting the Muslim community after Izzah's detention was announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Religious and community leaders must step forward to play an active role, through their speech and their deeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We were heartened to see that the National Council of Churches of Singapore (NCCS) had written a letter to MUIS, in support of our Muslim community − after the detention of Izzah, the radicalised female infant-care assistant, was announced.

sections.label: Religious leaders promoting integration
sections.summary: Religious and community leaders are encouraged to emphasise multi-racial and multi-religious values and organise activities with other religious groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Every religious and community leader has a role to play, within their own communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We strongly encourage religious leaders to emphasise multi-racial and multi-religious values in their teachings and the importance of the various communities in Singapore interacting, understanding and integrating with one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Religious leaders can also take the initiative to organise activities with other religious groups.

sections.label: Safeguarding common interaction space
sections.summary: People must actively befriend neighbours and co-workers, exchange greetings and celebrate festivals together to safeguard common space for interaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We made this point when we talked about schools earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We must make an active effort to make friends with our neighbours and co-workers, exchange greetings and celebrate our respective festivals together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We must safeguard and expand the common space where people from different races and religions can interact.

sections.label: Reporting radicalised foreigners question
sections.summary: A question asks what MHA does to encourage support mechanisms to report foreigners, noting the youngest of nine radicalised foreign domestic workers detected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What does MHA do to encourage those support mechanisms to report foreigners to the authorities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: She is the youngest among the nine radicalised foreign domestic workers that we have detected so far.

sections.label: Two repatriated Indonesian domestic workers
sections.summary: A 28-year-old single foreign domestic worker who worked in Singapore nearly five years and another from Indonesia were detected and repatriated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The other foreign domestic worker is 28 years old, single and had worked in Singapore for close to five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Both of them came from different parts of Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They were detected a few months ago and both were repatriated after investigations were complete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Both are not known to have influenced their friends or contacts in Singapore.

sections.label: EP Day counter-terrorism focus
sections.summary: EP Day focuses on counter-terrorism, guiding residents on suspicious behaviour and radicalised individuals, and encouraging SGSecure app subscription.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: EP Day now, as revamped, focuses a lot on counter-terrorism, making sure our residents living in Singapore and the heartlands are aware of what the nature of the risk is, helping to guide them on how to look out for suspicious behaviour and radicalised individuals and what to do, encouraging them to subscribe to the SGSecure app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: More than half a million phones have now got the SGSecure app and we are pushing it further.

sections.label: Threat of returning fighters
sections.summary: Colleagues and the speaker have discussed the threat of returning fighters from Syria and Iraq as they lose ground there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In various responses and speeches made by my colleagues and I, we have talked about the threat of returning fighters from Syria and Iraq as they begin to lose ground there.

sections.label: Radicalised people under 30
sections.summary: Those identified as radicalised tend to be younger people below 30 who look to the Internet for news and information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On the first question, on the profile, I have said earlier that those whom we have identified as radicalised tend to be younger people below the age of 30 who look to the Internet for a lot of news and information.

sections.label: Blocking sites and sensitising people
sections.summary: Sites are blocked when practical, but sensitising and inoculating people is more effective, with Government, community and religious groups reaching out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But I would like to say that in terms of blocking of sites, we do so when it is practical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But it would not be as effective or practical as sensitising and inoculating people from the false information and ideologies that are being conveyed through social media, and there are active steps being taken by the Government, community groups and religious organisations to reach out to people, including young people, to better inoculate the community against such influences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Yes, the answer is yes, we are working closely with the relevant associations.
